title: Priv EKS Terraform starter kits + safety latches for control plane provisioning
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Introduce a customer-friendly Terraform module bundle ("starter kits") and a set of runtime "safety latches" for Redwood Private EKS control plane provisioning. The intent is twofold: (1) provide plug-and-play examples and opinionated defaults so platform and infra engineers can stand up a Private control plane with minimal copy-paste; (2) embed operational guardrails (preflight checks, circuit-breaker style rollout latches, idempotent hooks, post-upgrade smoke tests, and automatic rollback playbooks) into the module to reduce upgrade risk and support faster recovery.
background: We continually see customers and solutions engineers creating bespoke bootstrap scripts and ad-hoc preflight steps. That produces inconsistent upgrades and a high support burden for Private deployments. This ticket bundles our best practices into sharable Terraform starter kits and a safety latch library that can be enabled per deployment. It aligns with Redwood's thesis of predictable serving and reduces oncall churn for Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Terraform module named redwood/priv-eks-starter (semver 0.1.0) published to our internal registry
Module exposes opinionated defaults that cover networking, control-plane nodegroups, KMS cross-account config, and minimal RBAC required for control plane lifecycle

Preflight action verifies VPC CIDR, route table reachability to control plane endpoints, required subnets, KMS key policy presence, and IAM role trust boundaries and fails clearly with remediation steps
Upgrade safety latch: module supports canary batch size + rollout pause + automatic health probe checks to abort and rollback using a documented playbook
Integrations: emits structured telemetry to Console (rollout id, batch progress, health signals) and wires to an observability dashboard template
Built-in post-upgrade smoke test set (kube-api, control-plane readiness, artifact reconcile) that runs automatically after canary batch and on-demand
Comprehensive docs + examples (quickstart for SRE, platform, and air-gapped on-prem guidance) added to Confluence and module README
E2E validation run passes in CI using a small dev account (run id included in comments)
tasks: Design starter kit layout and variables (networking, k8s version pin, KMS, SSO integration toggles)
Implement preflight validators as terraform-exec plan-time checks and remote-exec runners for advanced validations
Add upgrade safety latch primitives (canary percentage, pause window, health probe thresholds, rollback hook)
Instrument module to emit rollout events to Console via our control-plane telemetry schema
Add post-upgrade smoke test harness and make it optional via variable
Write docs and three quickstart examples (SRE, Platform, On-prem) and publish to Confluence
Create CI pipeline job to run module in a throwaway dev account and record results
Open PR to internal registry and capture review feedback
comments: 2026-01-18 Aisha Kumar: Created ticket. Initial problem statement and acceptance criteria drafted. Pitched starter kit concept in infra sync. Need alignment with SRE and Security before prototyping.

2026-01-21 Helen Zhao (SRE): Reviewed acceptance criteria; requested explicit SLA for canary pause windows and suggested adding a circuit-breaker that looks at API server error rate AND control-plane reconciliation lag.

2026-01-26 Diego Martinez: Spike complete — prototyped preflight checks as a combined terraform plan hook + aws-sdk validation. Found a race when KMS key is created concurrently from another account; added deterministic backoff and owner-tag verification.

2026-01-29 Security Review (note): Security requested KMS key policy templates and a recommended cross-account role trust boundary. Marked security_review_required = true and added policy snippets to the Confluence page.

2026-02-01 QA: Ran CI job in dev-account-3 (run id: ci-provision-20260201-03). Canary succeeded for k8s v1.28 on a single-node control plane; smoke tests passed except for a transient kube-controller-manager leader election flake — investigating timeout tuning.

2026-02-03 Diego Martinez: Addressed QA feedback; added leader-election probe with extended timeout as an opt-in variable. Drafted PR for internal registry. Noted remaining TODO: define rollout thresholds per-customer profile (low-risk/high-risk).
notes: This module aims to be the canonical starting point for customers adopting Redwood Private with minimal ops lift. Where customers have unique constraints we expect teams to fork the starter kit but retain safety-latch patterns. Track adoption metrics (module downloads/installs) and incidents during the first two quarters after release.
next_steps: Merge PR after Security + SRE signoff
Create customer-facing quickstart in Docs site
Plan a migration playbook for existing Private deployments to adopt safety latches
